name: C. H. Roberts (1909–1990)
contribution: First editor of 𝔓52 and the source of its famous early date.

name: Herbert Hunger (1914–2000)
contribution: Vienna Byzantinist who argued for an early 2nd-century 𝔓66.

name: T. C. Skeat (1907–2003)
contribution: With H. J. M. Milne, identified the scribes of Sinaiticus; later linked Sinaiticus and Vaticanus to Constantine’s order of Bibles.

name: Eric G. Turner (1911–1983)
contribution: Classified early codices by format and repeatedly cautioned against over-precise palaeographic dates.

name: Guglielmo Cavallo
contribution: Defined Biblical majuscule and its phases, the framework used for dating the great codices.

name: Pasquale Orsini & Willy Clarysse
contribution: Re-dated early New Testament papyri and criticised ‘theological palaeography’.

name: Brent Nongbri
contribution: Argues for wider, often later, date ranges (𝔓52, 𝔓66, Sinaiticus) and for radiocarbon testing.

name: Don Barker
contribution: Proposed the ‘graphic stream’ method for comparing like with like.

name: Stanley E. Porter
contribution: Defends mid-2nd-century dates for 𝔓52 and P.Egerton 2.

name: Larry W. Hurtado (1943–2019)
contribution: Studied early Christian manuscripts as artifacts (codex, nomina sacra, staurogram).

name: Philip W. Comfort
contribution: A leading advocate of early dates for the New Testament papyri.

name: D. C. Parker
contribution: Textual critic; author of the standard introduction and a study of Sinaiticus.

name: Mladen Popović
contribution: Leads the team combining radiocarbon with AI handwriting analysis (tested on the Dead Sea Scrolls).
